title: Inspect and recover Nucleus authentication
summary: Read account access or perform attended login while Nucleus preserves one managed credential authority and isolated job credentials.
use_when: Account access, managed credential concurrency, authentication contention, or attended recovery must be inspected or handled.
do_not_use_when: A requester wants to copy or refresh Nucleus's canonical credential or treat a live job as proof of bad authentication.
outcome: The account/readiness response is observed or a validated attended login advances Nucleus-owned authentication.
effects: Account reads can refresh and reconcile managed credentials without model work.
Attended login can replace the Nucleus-owned account credential after active authentication sessions finish.
authority: Nucleus owns its canonical managed credential and credential staging/promotion. Codex owns account-service behavior and payload meaning.
success: The supported account response and Nucleus readiness establish the requested observation; attended login promotes only a validated successful staged result.
failure_and_recovery: Treat authentication_busy as contention, not proof of invalid credentials. Quiesce requesters before attended recovery when work must remain uninterrupted.
Never restore older authentication bytes as part of program, service, or database rollback.
privacy: The canonical credential home and backups contain authentication material. Directory/file privacy requirements apply.
Host-managed authentication responses and managed-worker stderr are excluded from retained job output; managed refresh tokens never enter job homes.
does_not_authorize: Requester access to canonical credentials or rollback of a newer credential.
A service restart, unrelated account change, or interruption of active jobs without task authority.

consumers.statement: The current user and supported account readers may inspect authentication and perform separately attended recovery; requesters consume Nucleus execution without owning its credentials.

preconditions.statement: Use the private Nucleus credential authority and supported exact Codex adapter. Attended login requires exclusive authentication maintenance after active job and account sessions end.

inputs.statement: Account reads accept includeUsage and bounded waitSeconds; waitSeconds=0 is a nonblocking attempt. Attended device login is an explicit operator operation.
The managed home uses a private regular auth.json mode 0600 and a config.toml of at most 64 KiB containing only cli_auth_credentials_store = file.

outputs.statement: Account reads pass through Codex rateLimits and optional usage. Contention is authentication_busy; credential/account failure is model_auth_unavailable.
No job receives a managed refresh token or a writable canonical credential.

data_semantics.statement: An active job alone does not block an account read or prove an invalid credential. Account reads can refresh credentials without model work.
Managed jobs receive the current access token/account ID in memory; API-key jobs receive isolated key snapshots without copy-back.

identity_and_units.statement: One authoritative managed account credential lives under ~/Library/Application Support/Nucleus/codex-home with directory mode 0700. Canonical generations move only forward.
waitSeconds is seconds; Codex account rate-limit and usage payloads retain upstream meanings.
Nucleus defines no independent accounting units, prices, or billing semantics.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Account reads report the external account response for that invocation; health reports current Nucleus authentication readiness.
No account-response or service-availability objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Account reads can overlap jobs. Canonical refresh is serialized and staged privately; validated same-account credentials are atomically promoted. Concurrent refresh requests reuse an already advanced generation.

Started refresh and account reconciliation survive requester cancellation or timeout. Account reconciliation can promote a valid generation even when the account request fails. Attended login promotes only after successful validated completion.

No Codex child writes the authoritative file directly. Shutdown closes new account/refresh admission and waits for started authentication operations to settle. Credential recovery is separate from program/database rollback.

operational_limits.statement: There is one managed credential authority. Refresh tokens never enter job homes or output records; static API-key state never copies back.
No cross-user credential service or requester-managed canonical refresh is supported.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The exact Codex adapter and account service remain prerequisites. Imports occur under service coordination; program, database, and service rollback must not replace a newer credential.
No account-support or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Authentication and account reads rely on the exact adapter-proved Codex runtime and external account service; no installed Chancery contract covers that behavior.
